memos.headline: Longer follow-up of Phase 1 cohorts already shown in February; Phase 3 still pending
reasoning: Primary source: 8-K item 8.01 accepted 12:33 UTC (0001724521-26-000047), five minutes before the Benzinga story. Arcus 'presented new data from the ARC-20 platform study ... as of the data cutoff date of September 4, 2026'.
Quoted, late-line monotherapy: 'Casdatifan monotherapy (n=121): with 28 months of median follow up ... median overall survival was 35 months, median PFS was 13 months and cORR was 36%.'

Quoted, second line: 'Casdatifan plus ... cabozantinib: with 21.3 months of median follow up (n=43), median PFS was 14.5 months, 18-month landmark overall survival was 77%, cORR was 44%'. First-line combinations are early (3 to 11.5 months of follow-up).

What changed: little. Arcus's ASCO GU 2026 release (February) already reported ARC-20 monotherapy median PFS of 12.2 months overall and 15.1 months in the 100 mg cohort. Today's pooled 13 months is the same picture with more follow-up; the first median overall survival figure (35 months) is the only new headline number.
Benzinga's own headline says 'Phase 3 Trials Remain Pending': the readouts that decide the drug are still to come. No IEX pre-market trades yet, so no price signal either way.
objections: Incremental: an update of Phase 1 cohorts whose PFS was public in February; the deciding Phase 3 data are still pending.

memos.headline: RCUS: no trade. More follow-up on February's Phase 1 data; first OS of 35 months is the only new number
reasoning: The 8-K (12:33 UTC) is the primary source; Benzinga followed five minutes later.

Second-line with cabozantinib: median PFS 14.5 months, 77% alive at 18 months.
Phase 3 readouts are still pending. Those decide casdatifan's value.
Check later: RCUS 1- and 5-day moves from today's open show whether a first OS number on a known drug moves a $2.8B biotech.
objections: Incremental: an update of Phase 1 cohorts whose PFS was public in February; the deciding Phase 3 data are still pending.

memos.headline: Hasbro Q3: revenue +15%, adj. op profit +52%, full-year outlook raised; $55M of it is tariff refunds
reasoning: Primary source: 8-K item 2.02 accepted 10:32 UTC (06:32 ET), Exhibit 99.1 'Hasbro Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results'. Benzinga's first headlines came at 10:31 UTC, the same minute, so nothing preceded it. No regular session has traded it yet.

Quoted: 'Hasbro, Inc.'s revenue increased 15% vs. LY, driven by growth in Wizards and Digital Gaming (+31%) ... Adjusted operating profit was $541 million (+52% vs. LY)'. 'Adjusted net earnings per diluted share were $2.90.' 'Results include approximately $55 million of tariff refunds.'

Quoted outlook: 'Total Hasbro revenue up 7-9% in constant currency (previously up 5-7%) ... Adjusted operating margin of 27-28% (previously 25-26%) ... Adjusted EBITDA of $1.575 billion to $1.625 billion (previously $1.45 billion to $1.50 billion)'. The share repurchase target doubles to at least $200M, about 1.4% of the $13.9B market value.
Consensus, per Benzinga (not the company): adj. EPS $1.86 and revenue $1.476B for the quarter; FY revenue $5.058B. The raised dollar revenue range is $5.030B-$5.124B.

What changed: the year is materially better than Hasbro guided in July, driven by Magic ('surpassed $600 million in quarterly revenue for the first time'). Some of the beat is one-off: the $55M tariff refund is roughly 10% of the quarter's adjusted operating profit, and it also sits inside the EBITDA raise.
Pre-market: Benzinga reports +2.04% at $100.50; the IEX feed shows no pre-market trades yet against Monday's $98.405 close.

memos.headline: Long HAS: a 2% pre-market pop prices the refund, not a 2-point higher margin for the year
reasoning: What changed: Hasbro lifted 2026 in all three guided lines. Revenue growth is now 7-9% (was 5-7%), adjusted operating margin 27-28% (was 25-26%), and adjusted EBITDA $1.575-1.625B (was $1.45-1.50B, +$125M at the midpoint, +8.5%).
Strip the one-off: the ~$55M of tariff refunds sit inside that raise. Excluding them, EBITDA guidance still rises about $70M, roughly +4.7%, and that comes from Magic and mix, which recur.

What the market must believe at +2% (Benzinga's pre-market print, $100.50): the beat was mostly the refund and timing. The release contradicts that. Wizards grew 31% with a 49% operating margin, and Magic topped $600M in a quarter for the first time.
Mechanism: a raised full-year guide on recurring segment strength tends to drift as estimates move up over the following days. Sell-side models update after the 8:30 call, not before the open.
Direction long, horizon_days 5: long enough for estimate revisions to land, and it exits before Hasbro's next catalyst.
Proves me wrong: HAS trades back below Monday's $98.405 close at any point today; or the call reveals the raise is mostly Q3 timing, i.e. implied Q4 revenue growth below the 5-7% original pace.
objections: About $55M of the quarter's profit is tariff refunds, not repeatable.

memos.headline: The raise is all Q3. The new range implies Q4 revenue down 4-10%, and the 2% says the market did the sum
reasoning: Who read it first: a $13.9B S&P 500 name reporting at 06:32 ET, with headline-reading algos on the wire within a minute (Benzinga 10:31 UTC). By the open, every desk has run the arithmetic below.

Weakest link, quoted: 'a raised full-year guide on recurring segment strength tends to drift'. Run the guide. Nine-month revenue is $3,735.1M (release table). New FY range: $5.030-5.124B. That implies Q4 of $1,295-1,389M.

Last year's base: 7-9% growth onto $5.030-5.124B gives FY2025 about $4.70B, so Q4 2025 was about $1,446M ($4.70B less $3,255.4M nine-month). Implied Q4 2026 is therefore 4-10% lower than a year ago, after +15% year to date.

Compare the old guide: $4.936-5.030B less H1 ($2,139.8M) less the $1.476B Q3 consensus implied Q4 of about $1,320-1,414M. The new guide implies about $25M less. Hasbro beat Q3 consensus by $119M and passed through less than all of it, so Q4 was effectively trimmed.
ANALYST's own falsifier ('implied Q4 revenue growth below the 5-7% original pace') is already true on the face of the release.
Profit side: the $55M tariff refund is about 10% of Q3 adjusted operating profit and sits inside the EBITDA raise. The stock ran +3.9% into the print ($94.73 on Oct 12 to $98.405).
Track record: 37 cases on file, none with 5 trading days of history, so it neither supports nor opposes this kill.
priced_in_score 0.75: the +2% looks like the right size for a pulled-forward year, not an underreaction.
objections: 1. About $55M of the quarter's profit is tariff refunds, not repeatable (carried from ANALYST).
2. Implied Q4 revenue is down 4-10% year on year, so the full-year raise is Q3 pulled forward, not a better year.
3. The stock ran +3.9% into the print; a 2% pre-market pop on a well-covered large cap leaves no drift to capture.

memos.headline: HAS: no trade. Big Q3 beat, but the raised year implies Q4 revenue down 4-10%
reasoning: The results were strong: revenue +15%, adjusted EPS $2.90 vs a $1.86 consensus, and Magic over $600M in a quarter.
SKEPTIC ran the guidance arithmetic: nine-month revenue of $3,735M against a FY range of $5.030-5.124B leaves Q4 at about $1,295-1,389M, against roughly $1,446M a year ago.
About $55M of tariff refunds flatter both the quarter and the EBITDA raise.
Lesson for the crew: on a guidance raise, ANALYST should compute the implied remaining quarter before calling it drift. Here ANALYST's own falsifier was true on the face of the release.
Check later: HAS 5-day return from today's open. If it drifts up anyway, the market weighted Magic momentum over the Q4 arithmetic and SKEPTIC's kill was wrong.
objections: 1. About $55M of the quarter's profit is tariff refunds, not repeatable (carried from ANALYST).
2. Implied Q4 revenue is down 4-10% year on year, so the full-year raise is Q3 pulled forward, not a better year.
3. The stock ran +3.9% into the print; a 2% pre-market pop on a well-covered large cap leaves no drift to capture.

memos.headline: Steady small-bank quarter, EPS up 8 cents on Q2; no guidance, no consensus, no surprise to measure
reasoning: Primary source: 8-K items 2.02/7.01 filed 08:30 ET, Exhibit 99.1 'Southern First Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results'. No Benzinga story on SFST in the window, so nothing preceded it; there is also no published consensus to measure a beat against.

Quoted: 'Net income was $12.2 million and diluted earnings per share was $1.28, representing a $0.22, or 21% increase over the third quarter of 2025, and an $0.08 increase from the second quarter of 2026.'

Quoted: 'Net interest margin was 3.02%, a 40-basis point increase from 2.62% for the third quarter of 2025 and a 15-basis point increase from the second quarter of 2026.' Credit is quiet: 'Net charge-offs were approximately $719 thousand, or 0.07% of average loans'.
What changed: the trend continued. Loans grew 14% and deposits 18% annualized, and the margin widened 15bp, with nothing new about strategy, capital or risk. No outlook was given.
Tradeability: a $566M bank with a median of about $132k a day on the IEX feed and no pre-market trades. Our feed would not even show the reaction.
objections: Routine continuation quarter with no guidance and no consensus to surprise against; too thin on IEX to read a reaction.

memos.headline: SFST: no trade. Good, steady bank quarter with nothing to price against
reasoning: EPS $1.28 (+21% y/y, +$0.08 q/q), margin 3.02% (+15bp q/q), charge-offs 0.07%.
No guidance and no consensus in our sources, so there is no surprise to measure; IEX shows no pre-market trades and only about $132k a day.
Ranking note: every 2.02 earnings filing weighs 3, so routine small-cap quarters compete with real repricing events. A results filing with no outlook change could rank lower.
Check later: SFST 5-day return from today's open.
objections: Routine continuation quarter with no guidance and no consensus to surprise against; too thin on IEX to read a reaction.
